_provenance.note: Oklahoma citation authorities. Oklahoma's operative SNAP policy lives in Oklahoma Administrative Code (OAC) Title 340, Chapter 50 (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program), cited by section number, e.g. '340:50-11-111' (Categorically eligible household), '340:50-7-31' (Deductions), '340:50-5-100' (ABAWD). This pack writes 'OAC' before the section number in running text purely for cross-state disambiguation (matching this roster's general convention), while the regex below matches the bare '340:50-X-Y' form Oklahoma's own regulation uses natively. This pack ALSO cites Oklahoma Statutes Title 56 (Poor Persons) — a real, separate statute chapter, most consequentially 56 O.S. § 241.3 (Oklahoma's statutory bar on requesting an ABAWD waiver) — so this pack defines a SECOND citation family, '56 O.S. §', matching this roster's Kentucky, Alabama, and Louisiana packs' two-family pattern. This pack does NOT define a family for the 1997 session-law citation (1997 Okla. Sess. Laws ch. 414, §§ 28, 31) that two secondary sources cite for the drug-felony opt-out, since this pack could not independently verify those sections persist as currently-citable, standalone Title 56 law (see PROVENANCE.md Finding 3) — it is referenced in prose only, never as a machine-matched authority.

patterns.note: Oklahoma Administrative Code, Title 340 (Department of Human Services), Chapter 50 (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program), section number, e.g. 340:50-11-111 (Categorically eligible household), 340:50-7-31 (Deductions), 340:50-5-100 (ABAWD Work Requirements), 340:50-9-6 (Certification renewals).

Oklahoma Statutes, Title 56 (Poor Persons), cited by section number. This pack cites § 241, § 241.1, and — most consequentially — § 241.3 (Limitation of benefits), whose subsection (C) statutorily bars OKDHS from requesting an ABAWD waiver.

okoac.note: The application process — ordinary processing standard of no later than 30 calendar days
Household composition special cases — includes the elderly/disabled-member 165% FPL separate-household provision (Table III, Appendix C-3)

ABAWD (able-bodied adults without dependents) — 80 hours/month work requirement, 3-of-36-month time limit, age-exemption table last amended Aug. 15, 2024 (reflects the pre-OBBBA 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act figures, topping out at exempt-at-55; now stale relative to OBBBA's 18-64 standard)
Oklahoma Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Works (OK SNAP WORKS) — Oklahoma's branded SNAP Employment and Training program

Deductions — standard, earned income (20%), medical (actual expense minus $35, no flat shortcut), shelter (capped at Appendix C-3's figure absent an elderly/disabled member, uncapped with one), dependent care (no maximum), child support (ordinary deduction)
Determining the food benefit allotment — governs benefit calculation for categorically eligible households whose income exceeds the ordinary standard; cross-referenced by Appendix C-3's income tables
Changes after application and during the certification period — includes the minimum-allotment ($24) provision for 1-2 person categorically eligible households mid-certification
Procedures relating to food benefit certification renewals — establishes Oklahoma's flat 12-month standard certification period

Expedited service eligibility criteria — plain federal gates (gross income under $150 and liquid resources $100 or less; combined income/resources less than shelter costs; destitute migrant/seasonal farmworker) and the 7-calendar-day processing ceiling
Expedited service verification postponement — eligibility factors other than identity may be postponed when they cannot be verified within the 7-day expedited window

Categorically eligible household — TANF/SSI/2-1-1 Oklahoma pathways; removes both gross AND net income tests entirely with no stated percentage-of-FPL ceiling; subsection (f) lists what disqualifies categorical-eligibility status (lottery/gambling winnings, IPV, fleeing felon, work-registration noncompliance)

okstat.note: Participation in food stamp program — mandatory OKDHS duty to participate in the federal food stamp program
Electronic benefit identification program — implementation authority for Oklahoma's EBT system

Limitation of benefits — Amount and receipt of allotments. Subsection (A) states a stale pre-2023 ABAWD age band ('eighteen (18) years of age to fifty (50) years of age'), never amended since originally enacted 1997. Subsection (C), added by Laws 2013, c. 178, § 1, eff. Sept. 1, 2013, statutorily BARS OKDHS from ever requesting an ABAWD area waiver — this pack's flagship structural finding
Restrictions on debit and electronic benefit cards — bars EBT/TANF-funded card use at liquor stores, casinos, adult-entertainment establishments, and tobacco retailers
